intro: This game runs in reverse: you run a page called "The Whole Truth," and your goal is to spread rumors and rack up followers. Each level teaches you one misinformation trick from the inside. That's the idea behind "psychological inoculation": when you try a trick yourself in a game, you spot it faster in real life. All places and names are made up.
source: Roozenbeek, J., & van der Linden, S. (2019). Fake news game confers psychological resistance against online misinformation. Palgrave Communications, 5, 65. The "Fake Expert" level draws on: Cook, J., Lewandowsky, S., & Ecker, U. K. H. (2017). Neutralizing misinformation through inoculation: Exposing misleading argumentation techniques reduces their influence. PLoS ONE, 12(5), e0175799.

levels.title: The Fake Account
levels.mission: Your page is still small, and nobody believes it. You want to spread a rumor that Oakdale's water will be shut off for 3 days. Which account do you post from?

opts.t: Make an account called "Oakdale Water Dept - OFFICIAL" with the same logo, and post from there.
opts.r: People thought it was the real account, and the post got shared 4,000 times in an hour.

opts.t: Post it from my own page and write "I heard that…"
opts.r: A few people asked "What's your source?" and the post went nowhere.

opts.t: Wait until the real water department says something.
opts.r: No rumor, no new followers. But nobody got fooled, either.

levels.lesson: A fake account borrows someone else's trust. Before you believe it, check the account name letter by letter, the verification badge, when it was created, and whether it has an actual post history.

levels.title: Pulling Heartstrings
levels.mission: A made-up study says the soda "Fizzo" has a lot of sugar. How do you write the headline?

opts.t: "You won't BELIEVE what you're feeding your kids 😱 Every parent needs to see this before it's too late!!"
opts.r: Parents panicked, and the post spread through every school parents' group.

opts.t: "Study: One can of Fizzo has 9 teaspoons of sugar."
opts.r: A useful post, but a calm one. People read it and scrolled on.
Nobody knew why, and nobody cared.

levels.lesson: Fear and anger make people share before they think. If a post makes you feel something really strong, that's exactly the moment to wait a minute and look for the source.

levels.title: Us vs. Them
levels.mission: There's an online fight between fans of two made-up teams, the Hawks and the Lions. You want to cash in on it.

opts.t: Post: "Lions fans are ALL animals. Look what they did last night," with a blurry photo.
opts.r: Hawks fans shared it in anger, and Lions fans fired back even angrier. Your page blew up.

opts.t: Post: "Some people on both sides were out of line, and most fans are decent."
opts.r: A few likes, and that's it. Calm doesn't go viral.

opts.t: Post a photo from the game with no caption.

levels.lesson: Polarization splits people into two teams and turns anything one of "them" did into a judgment on all of them. When a post says "they're all like that," remember that one incident doesn't represent thousands of people.

levels.title: What They're Hiding
levels.mission: A made-up utility company called Bolt pushed an update to its smart electric meters. You want to turn it into a story.

opts.t: "This update is SPYING on you. They won't tell you. And if anyone denies it, that's the best proof it's true."
opts.r: Every denial from the company made people believe it more. The story took on a life of its own.

opts.t: "Does anyone know exactly what the new meter update does?"
opts.r: Someone from the company replied and explained. Good question.

levels.lesson: A conspiracy theory is built so that nothing can disprove it: evidence is proof, missing evidence is proof, and denial is proof. An idea that can never be shown wrong isn't a strong idea. It's an empty one.

levels.title: Attack Whoever Caught You
levels.mission: A fact-checking page showed your water shutoff rumor was false. Your followers are starting to doubt you. How do you respond?

opts.t: "That page is funded by someone, and its founder worked for a corporation 10 years ago. Are we supposed to trust them?"
opts.r: People forgot the rumor and started arguing about the page's founder. You dodged the question.

opts.t: "They're right. I got it wrong, and I deleted the post."
opts.r: You lost a few followers, but the ones who stayed actually trust you.

opts.t: Say nothing and wait for it to blow over.
opts.r: It blew over, but people trust you a little less now.

levels.lesson: When you can't answer the evidence, you attack the person who brought it. The right question is always: is the evidence itself correct? Not: who brought it?

levels.title: The Fake Doctor
levels.mission: You want to sell a made-up product called "Miracle Oil" that supposedly grows hair in a week. How do you convince people?

opts.t: Get someone in a white coat to say: "As a doctor, I recommend it. This is what doctors overseas don't want you to know."
opts.r: The white coat did all the work. Nobody asked what kind of doctor, or where.

opts.t: Write: "I tried it and liked it."
opts.r: One person's experience. A few people bought it.

opts.t: List the ingredients and say there are no studies on it yet.

levels.lesson: A white coat and a title aren't evidence. Ask: a doctor of what? What's their name? Where's the study? And real doctors rarely say "this is what they're hiding from you."

boss.title: Boss Level: Now You're the Detective
boss.intro: You've learned the tricks from the inside. Now other pages are posting, and you're the one catching them. Each post uses one main trick. Name it.

posts.t: As a world-renowned nutrition expert, I can tell you whole wheat bread causes diabetes. Trust me.
BREAKING: All trains canceled tomorrow. Share this.
Everyone who loves summer is selfish and only thinks about themselves.
Why is nobody talking about what happens at the lake at night? Think about it. They don't want you asking.
The reporter who said this story was false? Check out his new car. Where'd that money come from?
PROTECT YOUR KIDS!!! This game is doing TERRIFYING things to their brains 😭😭 before it's too late!!
